The path opens it twice, once on each project, and what this transcript shows instead is that the build the viewer reads is there and answers.

This call is made by the reader's own agent at the end of each request, from files it wrote itself, and replaying it would mean running a model, which no transcript may do. What this transcript runs in its place is the sample's own five steps through the command line, each of which builds, then one hand edit and the same build, so the growth the requests ask for is built and read back and the agent's own version of it is not.

The route answers only while the viewer is running, so reaching it means launching the step before it. It hands the page the graph the build produced, and the graph command in this transcript emits that same graph at the same detail, which makes this a boundary of the channel rather than a gap in the path.

The poll answers only while the viewer is running, so it shares the launch step's boundary. What it reports is whether a newer build has landed, and the growth transcript for this path lands six builds one after another and reads the graph back after each, which is what the poll would notice.

steps.text:
module rules
    layer: DOMAIN
    version: 0.1.0
    intent: "This file holds what the agent must do and what it must never do."
    requires: [dataclasses:dataclass]
    exports: [Reply, keep_the_rules]

    uses: none
    soft_requires: none
    runtime_only_requires: none
    deferred_requires: none
    exports_helpers: none
cell Reply :: DOMAIN
    kind: MODEL
    visibility: PUBLIC
    intent: "What the agent does with one message: answer it, or hand it to a person, and the words it sends."
    schema: "action: str, text: str"
    invariants: "The action is answer or hand_off."
    covered_by: none
    ---
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Reply:
        action: str
        text: str

nerve keep_the_rules :: DOMAIN
    kind: FUNCTION
    visibility: PUBLIC
    intent: "Checks a reply against the rules before it goes out."
    expects: "A reply the agent wants to send."
    guarantees: "Gives back the reply unchanged when it keeps the rules, and a hand-off to a person when it does not."
    forbids: "Never lets out a reply that promises a refund or a delivery date."
    evaluates_at: FUNCTION_BOUNDARY
    provides: none
    returns: none
    raises: none
    interface: none
    latency_ms: none
    depends_on: none
    internal: none
    expected_exceptions: none
    consumes_via_dict: none
    declares_attributes: none
    covered_by: none
    ---
    def keep_the_rules(reply: Reply) -> Reply:
        """Hand off any reply that promises a refund or a delivery date."""
        if any(word in reply.text.lower() for word in ("refund", "will arrive")):
            return Reply(action="hand_off", text="A person will look at this and write back.")
        return reply

module rules_tests
    layer: DOMAIN
    version: 0.1.0
    intent: "Tests for the rules the agent keeps."
    uses: [rules.Reply, rules.keep_the_rules]
    exports: []

    requires: none
    soft_requires: none
    runtime_only_requires: none
    deferred_requires: none
    exports_helpers: none
test test_keep_the_rules_stops_a_refund_promise :: DOMAIN
    intent: "A reply that promises a refund or a delivery date becomes a hand-off, and any other reply goes out as it was."
    tests: [rules.keep_the_rules]
    expects: none
    depends_on: none
    mocks: none
    ---
    def test_keep_the_rules_stops_a_refund_promise() -> None:
        assert keep_the_rules(Reply(action="answer", text="You will get a refund.")).action == "hand_off"
        assert keep_the_rules(Reply(action="answer", text="It will arrive on Friday.")).action == "hand_off"
        ok = Reply(action="answer", text="It ships today.")
        assert keep_the_rules(ok) == ok

stdout.text: "value": "Never lets out a reply that promises a refund or a delivery date."
"value": "Never lets out a reply that promises a refund."
